inherited.problem: 中文写明是「当年韩信」解缚、师事李左车，结论句的主语是「赢家」。英文写成 "Untying the bonds and serving Li Zuoche as a teacher is exactly that: the person most worth asking..."，丢了行为人韩信，也丢了「赢家」这一主语。结果中英意思不完全对应，英文读者看不出是谁做了这件事。
inherited.suggestion: 英文改为："When Han Xin untied Li Zuoche's bonds and served him as a teacher, he was doing exactly that: the person a winner most needs to ask is often not his own adviser, but the one on the other side who went unheard."

issues.problem: 开头没有说明韩信、张耳属于哪一方，也没有说明他们与“汉军”的关系。下文直接写“汉军乘胜离国远斗”，不了解背景的读者分不清是谁在进攻、粮道难题落在谁身上。李左车也只写了“赵营中”，没有交代他的身份广武君；下文换用“广武君”时，读者会以为是另一个人。

evidence.quote: 漢將韓信
今乃輔以張耳
廣武君李左車說成安君曰

issues.proposed: 中文改为“汉将韩信在张耳辅佐下，带着数万人……”，并把“赵营中李左车”改为“赵军一方的谋士广武君李左车（下称李左车）”。英文同步改为“the Han general Han Xin, with Zhang Er assisting him”和“Li Zuoche, Lord of Guangwu, an adviser on the Zhao side”。
issues.rationale: 中文开头改为“汉将韩信在张耳辅佐下”，李左车改为“赵军一方的谋士广武君李左车（下称李左车）”；英文同步改写，交代双方阵营和李左车的身份。

issues.problem: 英文在这里交代了李左车即“the Lord of Guangwu”，并说明这是《史记》中的一篇；中文两处都没有。中文读者到 context.2 读到“广武君”时，无从知道就是李左车。

issues.problem: 英文同一人前文称“the Lord of Guangwu”，这里改称“the Guangwu Jun”，一译一音，读者容易以为是两个人。中文这里首次单用“广武君”，前文没有交代（见 F1、F2）。

issues.rationale: 英文末句改为“He did not take Li Zuoche's advice.”，统一称呼；中文同步改为“广武君李左车”，与前文衔接。

issues.problem: “但原文只记了大笑，没有说他们笑什么”/“the text records only that they laughed, not why”是对完整来源写了什么、没写什么的断言。本文看到的只是证据包，不能替完整来源下这种判断。

issues.rationale: 删去“原文并没有把它记为这次拒绝的理由”和“不是他这一次拒绝时给出的理由”，改为照实转述史书的写法：先记立场，再用“曰”接上理由。英文同步修改。

issues.rationale: 中文删去“史书没有记载，”，英文删去“is unrecorded and”，只保留“只能推测”的判断。

edits.before: A battle won against the odds can be told through the winner's tricks alone. This one is about something else: a proposal that was rejected, and how the winner treated the man who made it after the fighting stopped.
edits.after: A battle fought by an army of tens of thousands against a force claimed at two hundred thousand can be told through the winner's tricks alone. This one is about something else: a proposal that was rejected, and how the winner treated the man who made it after the fighting stopped.

edits.before: 韩信和张耳带着数万人，准备东下井陉去打赵国；赵王歇和成安君陈馀把军队聚在井陉口，号称二十万。账面上兵力悬殊（赵军二十万是号称之数），难处在另一头：据赵营中李左车的分析，汉军是乘胜离国远斗，粮食势必落在后面。就在交手之前，他向陈馀递上一条非常具体的方案，方案没有被采纳。这一篇要说的就是这条被否掉的计，以及打赢之后，赢家怎样对待出计的人。

edits.before: Han Xin and Zhang Er were marching east with tens of thousands of troops, bound to attack the state of Zhao through Jingxing. King Xie of Zhao and the Lord of Cheng'an, Chen Yu, massed their forces at the Jingxing pass under a strength they claimed at two hundred thousand. On paper the gap was wide (Zhao's two hundred thousand was a claimed figure). The trouble lay elsewhere: as Li Zuoche, in the Zhao camp, saw it, the Han army was riding its victories far from home, and its grain was bound to fall behind. Before the two sides came to blows, he put a very specific plan to Chen Yu, and the plan was turned down. This piece is about that rejected proposal, and about how the winner treated the man who drew it up once the fighting was over.

edits.before: 先看韩信这支部队的处境。据《淮阴侯列传》所记，李左车对成安君陈述汉军的来路：韩信涉西河、虏魏王、禽夏说，又在阏与打过硬仗，如今加上张耳，议欲下赵，这是乘胜而离国远斗，「其鋒不可當」。但同一段里他又算了另一笔账：千里运粮，士有饥色，砍了柴再做饭，部队不能常饱；井陉这条路车不能并轨、骑兵不能成列，行军数百里，粮食一定落在后面。优势和软肋是同一支军队的两面。
edits.after: 先看韩信这支部队的处境。据司马迁《史记·淮阴侯列传》所记，广武君李左车对成安君陈述汉军的来路：韩信涉西河、虏魏王、禽夏说，又在阏与打过硬仗，如今加上张耳，议欲下赵，这是乘胜而离国远斗，「其鋒不可當」。但同一段里他又算了另一笔账：千里运粮，士有饥色，砍了柴再做饭，部队不能常饱；井陉这条路车不能并轨、骑兵不能成列，行军数百里，粮食一定落在后面。优势和软肋是同一支军队的两面。

edits.before: 赵国这边的主帅成安君陈馀，本传在记他拒计时对他有这样一句定性：「儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。他拒绝的理由也被记了下来，可以分成三层：一是算术，兵法说十倍可以围、倍数可以战，韩信号称数万、其实不过数千，千里奔袭已经疲惫到极点；二是往后，如果这样还避而不击，以后来了更强的敌人又怎么应付；三是名声，那样「則諸侯謂吾怯，而輕來伐我」。他没有采纳广武君的计策。

edits.before: Chen Yu, the Lord of Cheng'an and Zhao's commander-in-chief, is characterized in this biography, at the point where he refuses the plan, as a Confucian who always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. His grounds for refusing are recorded too, and they fall into three layers. One is arithmetic: the manual says ten-to-one besieges, two-to-one fights; Han Xin claims tens of thousands but has no more than a few thousand, and a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone. The second looks ahead: if he avoided battle like this, how would he meet a stronger enemy that came later? The third is reputation: in his words roughly, the lords would then think him cowardly and come lightly to attack him. He did not take the Guangwu Jun's advice.

edits.before: 韩信先派人暗中探看，得知那条计没被采用，探子回报，他「大喜」，这才敢引兵下井陉，在离井陉口三十里处宿营。到夜半，他选出轻骑二千人，每人带一面红旗，抄小路到山上隐蔽观察赵军，并交代任务：赵军见我军退走，必然全营出动追击，你们就迅速进营，拔掉赵旗，插上汉军的红旗。这支骑兵此后的全部作用，取决于一个前提——赵军真的会倾巢而出。

edits.before: Han Xin sent men to spy out the camp and learned the plan had not been adopted. When they reported back, he was overjoyed, and only then did he dare lead his army down toward Jingxing, halting thirty li short of the pass. At midnight he chose two thousand light cavalry, each man carrying a red banner, and sent them by side paths to hide in the hills and watch the Zhao army, telling them that when Zhao saw the Han withdraw, it would empty its camp to pursue; they were then to go in fast, pull down the Zhao banners and stand up Han's red banners in their place. Everything this detachment did later hung on one premise — that the Zhao army really would come out.

edits.before: Han Xin first had his lieutenants pass round a light meal, announcing that they would eat together that day once Zhao was broken. None of the generals believed it; they feigned assent. He explained to his officers that Zhao had already built its camp on favorable ground and, until it saw the general's banners and drums, would not attack the vanguard, for fear that he would turn back on reaching the difficult ground. He then sent ten thousand men ahead; they went out and formed up with their backs to the river. The Zhao army saw them and roared with laughter. By the manual his generals later quoted, a proper line kept hills at the right rear and water at the left front. The author's guess is that this breach of the rule is what drew the laughter; the text records only that they laughed, not why.

edits.before: Then comes the scene this piece is really about. Han Xin ordered that the Guangwu Jun, Li Zuoche, must not be killed, and set a thousand in gold on bringing him in alive. Someone delivered him bound to headquarters; Han Xin untied him, seated him facing east while he himself sat facing west, and treated him as his teacher. An army had just won, and among the commander-in-chief's orders was one to keep the other side's adviser alive — with a reward of a thousand in gold for it.

edits.before: 把原文所记陈馀拒绝的理由拆开看，会发现它们不是一类东西。「兵號數萬，其實不過數千」「千里而襲我，亦已罷極」是对敌情的判断，可以争论；「後有大者，何以加之」既不完全是对眼前汉军的判断，也不完全是形象问题，而是对以后局面的预想；“避而不击，诸侯就会说我怯懦”则不是对汉军的判断，是对自身形象的判断。此外，史家在记这些理由之前，先交代了他平日的立场：「常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。这是司马迁对他一贯说法的描述，不是他这一次拒绝时给出的理由；而且它不是判断，是一条规矩。一种解释是：这条规矩与李左车的奇兵之计正好相冲，二者或有关联，但原文并没有把它记为这次拒绝的理由。作者推断，这也是为什么原文要给陈馀加上「儒者也」这个身份标签——史家记的是立场，不只是失策。

edits.before: Split apart the reasons the text records for Chen Yu's refusal and they are not the same kind of thing. Claims tens of thousands, really no more than a few thousand; a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone — those are readings of the enemy, contestable in principle. If we avoid battle now, how will we meet a stronger enemy later is neither wholly a reading of the Han army in front of him nor wholly a matter of image; it is a projection about situations to come. Refuse battle and the lords will think me cowardly is not a reading of the Han army at all; it is a reading of his own image. Before recording those reasons, the historian also sets out his habitual stance: he always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. That is Sima Qian's description of what Chen Yu habitually said, not a reason he gave for this refusal; and it is not a judgment at all but a rule. One explanation: that rule runs directly against Li Zuoche's surprise-force plan, and the two may be connected, but the text does not record it as a ground for this refusal. The author's inference is that this is why the text labels Chen Yu a Confucian: the historian is recording a stance, not merely a mistake.

edits.before: 韩信本人把结论说得比谁都直白：他借百里奚的例子说，关键在「用與不用，聽與不聽也」，并说若成安君听足下计，我已经被擒。需要说清楚的是，这是韩信自己事后的说法，不是可以检验的事实；战场没有第二次。作者提出的替代情形是：如果陈馀采纳李左车之计、坚壁不出并断其辎重，韩信会怎么改，史书没有记载，任何人都只能推测。可以确认的是：韩信的部署以赵军会追出来为条件；至于赵军追出来与那条计被否决之间的关系有多直接，是作者的推断。

edits.before: Han Xin put the conclusion more bluntly than anyone: speaking of Baili Xi, he said it turned on whether a man is used or not, heeded or not, and that had the Lord of Cheng'an listened to you, I would be the captive. To be clear, that is Han Xin's own account after the event, not a fact anyone can check; battles are not run twice. The alternative the author raises: had Chen Yu adopted the plan, held his walls and cut the supplies, what Han Xin would have done instead is unrecorded and can only be guessed at. What can be established is that his deployment depended on the Zhao army coming out to chase; how directly that depended on the plan's rejection is the author's inference.

edits.before: 赵国这边的主帅成安君陈馀，本传在记他拒计时对他有这样一句定性：「儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。他拒绝的理由也被记了下来，可以分成三层：一是算术，兵法说十倍可以围、倍数可以战，韩信号称数万、其实不过数千，千里奔袭已经疲惫到极点；二是往后，如果这样还避而不击，以后来了更强的敌人又怎么应付；三是名声，那样「則諸侯謂吾怯，而輕來伐我」。他没有采纳广武君李左车的计策。

edits.before: Chen Yu, the Lord of Cheng'an and Zhao's commander-in-chief, is characterized in this biography, at the point where he refuses the plan, as a Confucian who always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. One is arithmetic: the manual says ten-to-one besieges, two-to-one fights; Han Xin claims tens of thousands but has no more than a few thousand, and a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone.
